svg.title: Skier on slope with force components
svg.desc: A skier descends left down a 25° slope. Weight w points vertically down, normal force N points outward, and friction f points uphill. Dashed weight components w perpendicular and w parallel sum to w. The x axis points downhill and the y axis outward. The free-body diagram repeats the same three forces; N and w share one scale, and the 45 N friction is enlarged so it stays visible. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Gravity and kinetic friction determine the skier’s acceleration
Blue N; red weight (same scale); green friction × 5

Book example: 62 kg, 25° slope, 45 N friction. Illustrative initial speed 1 m/s; no air drag. Equal
intervals are equal model times. N balances the perpendicular weight component.
